bt.audioHint: Headphones and speakers also appear in Sound once they are connected.
bt.err.authFailed: Pairing failed: the code did not match or the device refused it.
bt.err.blocked: Bluetooth is turned off by a hardware or software switch (rfkill).
bt.err.failed: The device did not respond. Make sure it is on and nearby.
bt.err.noProfile: Paired, but the device offers no service LordOS can connect to (audio, input).
bt.nearbyHint: Put the device in pairing mode to see it here.
bt.noAdapter: This computer has no Bluetooth adapter.
bt.noAgent: LordOS could not register as the pairing agent: devices that ask for a code may not pair.
bt.noService: The Bluetooth service (bluez) is not running or not installed.
bt.offHint: Turn on Bluetooth to connect headphones, keyboards, mice and other devices.
bt.prompt.authorize.body: “{name}” wants to pair with this computer.
bt.prompt.authorize.title: Bluetooth Pairing Request
bt.prompt.confirm.body: Make sure this code matches the one shown on “{name}”.
bt.prompt.confirm.title: Pair with “{name}”?
bt.prompt.display-passkey.body: Type this code on “{name}”, then press Return on it.
bt.prompt.display-passkey.title: Pairing with “{name}”
bt.prompt.display-pin.title: Pairing with “{name}”
bt.prompt.passkey.title: Pairing with “{name}”
bt.prompt.pin.body: Enter the PIN for “{name}” (often 0000 or 1234; check its manual).
bt.prompt.pin.title: Pairing with “{name}”
bt.prompt.service.body: “{name}” wants to use a service on this computer.
bt.prompt.service.title: Allow “{name}”?
bt.title: Bluetooth
defaults.failed: Could not save the choice in ~/.config/mimeapps.list.
defaults.filesHint: Files opens documents with these apps when you double-click them, and lists them first in “Open With”.
defaults.footer: Shared with Linux apps (GNOME, KDE, xdg-open) through ~/.config/mimeapps.list.
defaults.none: No installed app can open these
display.arrangeHint: Drag a display to place it next to the others. The white bar marks the main display (menu bar and Dock).
display.captureHint: What screenshots, screen recording and the remote desktop see.
display.failed: That mode could not be used. The previous one is still active.

display.keepBody.one: Your display settings will go back to the previous ones in {count} second.
display.keepBody.other: Your display settings will go back to the previous ones in {count} seconds.

display.menuBarAll: Show menu bar on all displays
display.multipleHint: Extend makes one desktop across every display: windows move between them and can span two. Mirror shows the main display on all of them.
display.noBacklight: This display does not offer brightness control (external monitors and virtual machines).
display.noCrtc: {connector}: connected, but the graphics card cannot drive another display
display.notOnMonitor: This session is not on the monitor right now (it is being viewed from the network), so its displays cannot be changed. Night Shift settings still apply when it returns.
display.rotationHint: A rotated screen is composed by the CPU.
display.scaleHint: Text, icons and images are drawn at the display's own resolution, so every scale stays sharp. Linux apps with fractional scaling render at it too.
display.unavailable: The display information is not available.
night.customHint: Night Shift turns on and off at these times every day.
night.footer: Night Shift shifts the colors of your display to the warmer end of the spectrum after dark.
night.noSun: The sunset time is not known for this time zone: Night Shift uses 22:00 to 07:00.
night.offHint: Use the switch below to turn it on until tomorrow.
night.software: This display has no color table (gamma LUT), so Night Shift tints the image by software.
night.sunHint: Today: from {set} to {rise}, for your time zone. Your location is never looked up on the network.
night.title: Night Shift
notif.allowPackage: The same as the “Notifications” permission in Privacy & Security.
notif.appsFooter: Apps appear here after they send their first notification. Linux apps (GTK, Qt) notify through the standard freedesktop service.
notif.dndFooter: While Do Not Disturb is on, notifications are kept silently and no banners are shown.
notif.groupingHint: Several banners from the same app are shown as one.
notif.lockScreenHint: The lock screen does not show notifications yet.
notif.styleHint.alert: Alerts stay on screen until you dismiss them.
notif.styleHint.banner: Banners go away on their own after a few seconds.
power.buttonsHint: Handled by the system (systemd-logind) for every user.
power.degraded: Performance mode is limited right now (the computer is too hot or on a lap).
power.lidAC: When the lid is closed on power adapter
power.lock: Require password after the display turns off
power.menuPercent: Show percentage in the menu bar
power.modeGovernor: Without power-profiles-daemon: sets the CPU frequency governor (now: {gov}).
power.needAdmin: Only an administrator can change this.
power.noBattery: This computer runs on power from the wall (no battery).
power.noProfiles: Not available: install power-profiles-daemon, or this CPU does not allow changing its frequency.
power.offAC: Turn display off on power adapter when inactive
power.offBattery: Turn display off on battery when inactive
power.powerKey: When the power button is pressed
power.screenSleepHint: Counted from the last time the keyboard, mouse or trackpad was used.
power.sleepAC: Sleep on power adapter when inactive
time.needAdmin: Only an administrator can change the date, the time and the time zone.
time.synced: Synchronized with the network time servers (systemd-timesyncd).
time.zoneFooter: Chosen by hand: LordOS never looks up your location on the network.
